title: Jassa Singh’s Mother, Devotion, and Initiation into the Khalsa

blocks.text: Jassa Singh is introduced through the disciplined devotion of his household, especially his mother, who comes from initiated Sikh parents and has been formed by daily recitation, singing, and reverence for Gurbani. The future leader first appears in an atmosphere of prayer rather than war, where mother and son are bound together through sacred routine and public devotion.

Their piety draws them toward the assembled Khalsa, and the sangat receives them with warmth when they come to pay homage. The narrative stresses that the mother-son pair do not arrive seeking status, but as sincere devotees whose reverence naturally brings them into the orbit of the Panth.

Kapoor Singh then draws the child close, initiates him into the Khalsa, and begins training him through humble duty. Jassa Singh is assigned to distribute feed to the horses, a lowly task that nevertheless marks the beginning of disciplined service under Khalsa care.
